Commit 4ff09db1b79b (""bpf: net: Change sk_getsockopt() to take the
sockptr_t argument"") made it possible to call sk_getsockopt()
with both user and kernel address space buffers through the use of
the sockptr_t type.  Unfortunately at the time of conversion the
security_socket_getpeersec_stream() LSM hook was written to only
accept userspace buffers
column2: and in a desire to avoid having to change

column1: the LSM hook the commit author simply passed the sockptr_t's
userspace buffer pointer.  Since the only sk_getsockopt() callers
at the time of conversion which used kernel sockptr_t buffers did
not allow SO_PEERSEC
security_socket_getpeersec_stream() hook
also very fragile as future changes presented the possibility of
silently passing kernel space pointers to the LSM hook.
There are several ways to protect against this
code review of future commits
column2: but since relying on code review to

column1: catch bugs is a recipe for disaster and the upstream eBPF maintainer
is ""strongly against defensive programming""
LSM hook
column2: and all of the implementations to support sockptr_t and

column1: safely handle both user and kernel space buffers.
